observation_summary: The StringUtils methods (containsAny, indexOfAny, containsNone, etc.) fail to correctly handle Unicode supplementary characters (which are represented as surrogate pairs in Java). The methods treat the high and low surrogates as individual characters, leading to incorrect matching logic.
hypothesis: The existing algorithms for searching characters in strings iterate through the string character-by-character without accounting for surrogate pairs. When a high surrogate is encountered, the algorithm should check if it is part of a supplementary character pair and validate the subsequent low surrogate before confirming a match.
prediction: The code will be updated to detect high surrogates using Character.isHighSurrogate(ch) and, upon finding one, perform an additional check on the next character (the low surrogate) to ensure the entire supplementary character is matched correctly.
experiment_rationale: The fix diff shows the introduction of logic to check for high surrogates and validate the subsequent character in the string and search array, which confirms that the original procedural logic was insufficient for handling multi-char Unicode representations.
reasoning_summary: The defect is a failure in the computational logic of the search methods. The methods were correctly iterating through the string but lacked the necessary logic to handle the specific data structure of Unicode supplementary characters (surrogate pairs). This is a classic algorithmic correction where the procedure for identifying a match was updated to include the correct handling of surrogate pairs.
evidence_used: The fix_diff_oracle shows the addition of Character.isHighSurrogate(ch) checks and logic to compare the next character (cs.charAt(i + 1)) in multiple methods.
The bug report explicitly mentions that the methods fail to handle Unicode 2.0+ supplementary characters correctly.
The failing tests confirm that the methods return incorrect results when supplementary characters are involved.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the fix adds checks, these are not simple guard clauses or validation checks; they are integral parts of the search algorithm's logic to correctly identify a match.
This is a local procedural correction within existing methods, not a design-level capability gap.
